hero.lead: A nation of 11.5 million in one of the driest lands on earth, where every home cooks with clean fuel and the World Bank approved $700 million for private investment in 2026.

capital.heading: Jordan keeps its reforms on schedule. Next, every child reading by ten.

register.name: Eurobond due 2032
register.detail: Announced 4 November 2025 · Seven years · Coupon 5.75% · Orders above three times the issue
register.note: Refinanced the 6.125% Eurobond of 2015 at a lower cost
register.text: A seven-year Eurobond at 5.75%, 1.75 points below the 2023 issue. Jordan used it to buy back $388 million of its 2015 Eurobond early in November 2025 and repaid the remaining $612 million in January 2026. Cheaper debt leaves more of the budget for the seven standards.

register.name: Jordan Growth and Competitiveness Development Policy Financing II
register.note: Reforms to draw private investment and create jobs
register.text: World Bank budget support for reforms that make it easier and cheaper to do business, extend social protection to flexible and part-time workers, and open electricity transmission, generation and storage to private investment. It also widens access to finance for micro, small and medium firms, which make up about 99 percent of businesses. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Extended Fund Facility and Resilience and Sustainability Facility
register.note: About $1.3 billion EFF and $700 million RSF; about $188 million released in June 2026
register.text: A four-year programme approved in January 2024, with a climate facility added in June 2025.

register.name: Aqaba-Amman Water Desalination and Conveyance Project (FP288)
register.detail: Approved 30 October 2025 · $220 million loan and $75 million grant · Accredited entity IFC
register.note: Loan and grant for the National Water Carrier
register.text: Green Climate Fund financing for the National Water Carrier, which is to meet about 40 percent of Jordan’s municipal water needs by 2030. The National Water Carrier will desalinate 300 million cubic metres of Red Sea water a year at Aqaba and pump it some 438 km north to Amman and other governorates. It serves the water standard.

register.name: Jordan Growth and Competitiveness Development Policy Financing
register.detail: Approved 8 April 2025 · Part of a $1.1 billion package
register.note: Investment, exports and jobs, especially for young people and women
register.text: World Bank budget support for reforms to the business environment, competition, access to finance and customs, so that firms invest, export and hire. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Resilient and Sustainable Social Protection Program
register.detail: Approved 8 April 2025 · Part of a $1.1 billion package
register.note: Cash transfers for 1.2 million people; health insurance for 150,000
register.text: World Bank financing for cash transfers to 1.2 million vulnerable people, health insurance for 150,000 and early warning for 1 million. It links social protection to schools, clinics and jobs, and serves the food, health and livelihood standards.

register.name: Electricity Sector Efficiency and Supply Reliability Program, additional financing
register.detail: Approved 8 April 2025 · Part of a $1.1 billion package
register.text: World Bank financing for cost savings and revenue in the power sector, energy efficiency in public institutions and the cybersecurity of transmission. It supports Jordan’s target of 31 percent renewable electricity by 2030 and serves the energy standard.

register.name: Innovative Startups and SMEs Fund (ISSF 2.0)
register.detail: Approved 8 April 2025 · Five years · Part of a $1.1 billion package
register.note: About $150 million of private capital, 100 startups, 1,500 jobs
register.text: World Bank financing for a fund that invests alongside private investors in startups in technology, finance, green technology and health technology, mainly led by women and young people. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Arab Fund financing for the National Water Carrier
register.note: The electricity supply for the water carrier
register.text: An Arab Fund for Economic and Social Development loan for the power supply of the National Water Carrier, signed with the Ministry of Finance and the National Electric Power Company. It also lets the national grid take more generation, including renewables. It serves the water and energy standards.
by: Arab Fund for Economic and Social Development

register.name: EIB financing for the Aqaba-Amman Water Desalination and Conveyance Project
register.detail: Five signatures, 8 December 2022 to 24 July 2025 · Includes EU investment grants
register.note: 300 million cubic metres of drinking water a year for Amman
register.text: European Investment Bank financing, with European Union investment grants, for the National Water Carrier. The first EUR 200 million soft loan was the first financing agreement signed for the project; the bank has proposed about EUR 874 million in all. It serves the water standard.

register.name: DFC loan and political risk insurance for the National Water Carrier
register.detail: Before the DFC Board 16 September 2026 · Loan up to $1 billion · Insurance up to $800 million
register.note: Water for at least 4 million people
register.text: The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation’s loan to the National Carrier Project Company, and political risk insurance for its investors. The U.S. Department of State has separately approved a $300 million grant. The National Water Carrier will desalinate 300 million cubic metres of Red Sea water a year at Aqaba and pump it some 438 km north to Amman and other governorates.

register.name: Housing Bank blue bond
register.detail: July 2026 · EBRD investment $100 million · Programme of $200 million
register.note: The first blue bond in Jordan and the southern and eastern Mediterranean
register.text: The EBRD bought $100 million of blue bonds issued by the Housing Bank, whose proceeds go to water and wastewater projects, mainly the National Water Carrier. It brings local capital markets into the water standard.

register.name: IFC financing for the Aqaba-Amman Water Desalination and Conveyance Project
register.detail: Approved 19 February 2026 · Pending signing · A loan up to $375 million and $32 million of risk management
register.note: A 30-year concession with a 280 MW solar plant
register.text: IFC financing for the private project company that will design, finance, build and run the desalination plant, the 438 km pipeline and a solar plant of about 280 MW under a 30-year concession, after which the assets pass to the Government. It serves the water standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 93 in every hundred live in towns and cities; the rest live on the land they farm and fish.
items.alt: A street in downtown Amman, Jordan

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in farms and pasture
items.text: The land that feeds the nation, and the first place a citizen dividend can be earned.
items.alt: Farmland in the Jordan Valley, Jordan

items.name: The Cities
items.label: Live in towns and cities
items.text: Dense cities make every pipe, cable and clinic serve more people for each dollar spent.
items.alt: The white stone hillside city of Amman, Jordan, at dusk

items.name: The Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water per person
items.text: Below the scarcity line of 1,000 cubic metres: every drop must be stored, treated and reused.
items.alt: The Dead Sea shore, Jordan, salt formations and still water

items.name: The Power
items.label: Of energy from renewables, 2021
items.text: Sun, wind, water and biomass already carry part of the load; the rest is the opportunity.
items.alt: A large solar park in the desert of Jordan

items.name: Microfund for Women
items.text: The largest microfinance institution in Jordan, serving more than 120,000 clients through 63 branches, 45 of them outside Amman, with a focus on women-led businesses. The EBRD, the EU and the Green Climate Fund lent it US$4 million for green lending in 2025.
